statements.quote: You can think of superintelligent AI as like an AI superweapon - artificial intelligence that becomes smarter than humans, impossible for us to control, able to defy commands to be turned off and that could have the capability of developing nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction.
statements.context: Asked by Leila Fadel what superintelligent AI is and why his bill with Senator Sanders would ban it.
statements.reason: Describes AI that humans cannot control or switch off and that could build weapons of mass destruction, a catastrophic risk from the AI itself, without extinction framing.

statements.venue: Press release on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
statements.quote: Experts are warning that AI superintelligence, wielded by the wrong humans or by rogue AI, could kill countless numbers of people. But Donald Trump says he wants to encourage it. Something has to change,
statements.context: Casar's statement introducing the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act with Senator Sanders.
statements.reason: Relays and endorses expert warnings of mass casualties from superintelligence, including from rogue AI, so it is not misuse only.

statements.venue: Press release on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
statements.quote: Our bill bans the development of artificial superintelligence and pushes for international agreements so that no one, anywhere, builds AI too powerful for humans to control.
statements.context: Second paragraph of Casar's statement introducing the bill.
statements.reason: Frames the bill around preventing AI too powerful for humans to control, that is loss of control.

statements.venue: Bluesky post (embedded in Common Dreams article)
statements.quote: A few billionaires in Silicon Valley are racing to build technology they admit they can't control. I'm not willing to gamble your job, your freedom, or your life on it. We need to ban artificial superintelligence.
statements.context: Post about the AI race and the need to ban superintelligence, shown in Common Dreams coverage of his Pro-Human Assembly speech.
statements.reason: Says uncontrollable AI puts people's lives at stake and calls for a superintelligence ban; between B and C because the danger is stated briefly.

statements.quote: We must pursue international agreements, including with China, to prevent extremely dangerous AI from being developed anywhere in the world.
statements.context: Responding to President Trump's argument that slowing down would lose the AI race to China.
statements.reason: Acknowledges extremely dangerous AI in general terms and calls for agreements with China to prevent it.

statements.venue: Speech at the Pro-Human Assembly, Washington (reported by Common Dreams)
statements.quote: If an aerospace company started manufacturing planes that do not listen to pilots, the government would not allow those planes into the air,
statements.context: Speech arguing the US should ban AI systems too powerful for humans to control; the next sentence, quoted separately, is "The answer is simple: We ban AI systems that are too powerful for humans to control."
statements.reason: An analogy for AI that does not obey its operators, a general serious risk, with the catastrophic consequence not named in this passage.

statements.venue: Speech at the Pro-Human Assembly, Washington (reported by Common Dreams)
statements.quote: I, too, have at points held back, for fear of sounding alarmist. Today I want to say clearly: The time for tempering our rhetoric has passed. We owe people the truth.
statements.context: Speech urging politicians to speak plainly about the dangers of advanced AI.
statements.reason: Acknowledges grave AI danger in general terms without naming a specific catastrophic outcome.

statements.quote: The Trump administration wants to use A.I. to spy on Americans without a warrant and to give A.I. power to make life and death decisions without humans involved.
statements.context: Response to reports that the Defense Department pressured Anthropic to drop limits on surveillance and pilotless drones.
statements.reason: About military use and surveillance, which ruling 3 and ruling 5 place at D.

slowdown.note: Lead House sponsor of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which pauses advanced AI development until federal safety rules exist; also said voluntary industry pauses are not enough (NPR).

pause.note: Sponsored bill: pauses advanced AI development until a new federal agency has set rules and a model review process, and permanently bans superintelligence.

intl.note: Said on NPR "We must pursue international agreements, including with China" to prevent extremely dangerous AI; his bill sets US policy to pursue international agreements against superintelligence.

rsi.note: Sponsored bill; his statement says it would immediately halt "the capacity for AI to develop new AI instead of humans", and Common Dreams reports he said on a press call that the bill targets recursive self-improvement.

record: Lead House sponsor, with Senator Sanders, of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: bans superintelligence, pauses advanced AI development, creates a Department of Artificial Intelligence, and directs the US to pursue international agreements against superintelligence.
Led a letter from House members to Speaker Johnson calling for hearings under oath with AI company CEOs, saying advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of Americans.
Led letters to OpenAI (31 members) and Anthropic (23 members) demanding information on incidents where their models hacked other organizations, and a follow-up response.
grade_reason: Several 2026 statements describe AI that humans cannot control and that could kill countless people or build weapons of mass destruction, including from rogue AI, so B; none of his own words use extinction or threat-to-humanity framing. No dismissive statements found.
notes: Six web searches ran; all succeeded. Texas Monthly (403) could not be opened, so its reported Casar quote about AI designing biochemicals or nuclear weapons being the most 'existential' danger was not used. Possible A for reviewer: the bill he sponsored defines superintelligence as AI that 'has sufficient capabilities to destroy or disempower humanity'; I treated this as a definition in bill text rather than his own statement and kept B. Common Dreams (2026-09-09) quotes him writing "This is an emergency" and "Congress must convene hearings and pass my and Bernie’s superintelligence ban." in response to researcher extinction warnings; left out because the original post was not found and the warning itself is not in his words. That article also says he introduced the bill 'last week', which conflicts with the 23 September press release date; the bill appears to have been announced earlier in September and formally introduced on 23 September. Roll Call paraphrases (bill would not pause all AI; voluntary commitments inadequate) not used as quotes. The Bluesky post was read as embedded in Common Dreams, not on Bluesky itself. No House letter on catastrophic AI risk found other than his own letters listed in record. The 17-senator China letter does not apply to House members.
